newsitem.title: SENEGAL: U.S. peacekeeping trainers arrive in Senegal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. peacekeeping trainers arrive in Senegal.

text.p: Sixty U.S. military trainers have arrived in Senegal to instruct Senegalese troops who will form part of a planned African peacekeeping force, U.S. embassy sources said on Monday.
The Group of Eight industrialised countries agreed at a summit meeting in Denver last month to support an African Crisis Response Initiative (ACRI).
Senegal and Uganda could be among the first group of African countries to take part in the ACRI with battalion-size units.
The U.S. trainers arrived on Sunday from the Third Special Forces Group in Fort Bragg, North Carolina, and 100 U.S. troops arrived in Uganda on Monday to train soldiers there.

Senegal has taken part in several peacekeeping missions, notably in Lebanon, Liberia and Rwanda. Its soldiers are among the U.N. forces that have been monitoring the Kuwait-Iraq border since the end of the 1991 Gulf War.

Senegalese General Charles Andre Nelson has been appointed to command an African peacekeeping force that could operate in the Congo Republic's capital, Brazzaville, if talks now going on lead to a durable truce between warring political parties there.
